rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir omits the hamza in al-Qurʾān whether definite or indefinite; deriving the reading from q-r-n is judged weak.
rows.anchor: وترك ابن كثير همزة القرآن مع التعريف والتنكير حيث وقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudan is accusative as a circumstantial qualifier of the Qurʾān.
rows.anchor: وهدى في موضع نصب على الحال من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The whole Qurʾān, including clear and ambiguous, abrogating and abrogated passages, is guidance; bayyināt specifies lawful and unlawful rulings, admonitions, and decisive verses.
rows.anchor: فالمراد أن القرآن بجملته من محكم ومتشابه وناسخ ومنسوخ هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-hudā is anaphoric, referring back to earlier guidance.
rows.anchor: فالألف واللام في الهدى للعهد والمراد الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-furqān is that which distinguishes truth from falsehood.
rows.anchor: والفرقان المفرق بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahida means present; al-shahr is temporal, meaning presence in town during the month.
rows.anchor: وشهد بمعنى حضر، والشهر نصب على الظرف

rows.speaker: الحسن وعيسى الثقفي والزهري وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وأبو حيوة
rows.claim: These readers vocalize the lām of fal-yasumhu; they similarly read every imperative lām in the Qurʾān with its original kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وعيسى الثقفي والزهري وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي وأبو حيوة «فليصمه»

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس وعبيدة السلماني
rows.claim: Whoever was resident when Ramadan began must complete the fast even if he later travels; only one already traveling when Ramadan begins may break it.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس وعبيدة السلماني: من شهد أي من حضر دخول الشهر

rows.speaker: جمهور الأمة
rows.claim: The majority require fasting while resident if one witnesses either the beginning or end of the month.
rows.anchor: وقال جمهور الأمة: من شهد أول الشهر أو آخره فليصم ما دام مقيما

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: Abu Hanifa and his companions require legal capacity during the month; insanity throughout Ramadan entails no make-up, while insanity at its beginning or end requires making up those days.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حنيفة وأصحابه: من شهد الشهر بشروط التكليف غير مجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Abu Hanifa’s interpretation, al-shahr is the direct object of shahida.
rows.anchor: ونصب الشهر على هذا التأويل هو على المفعول الصريح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Or on a journey” functions like “or traveling,” so it coordinates with a noun.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: أو على سفر بمنزلة أو مسافرا

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن القعقاع ويحيى بن وثاب وابن هرمز وعيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: These readers pronounce the sīn of al-yusr and al-ʿusr with ḍamma; the majority leave it quiescent.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر بن القعقاع ويحيى بن وثاب وابن هرمز وعيسى بن عمر «اليسر» و «العسر»

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك بن مزاحم
rows.claim: Mujahid and al-Dahhak identify ease with breaking the fast while traveling and hardship with fasting during travel.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد والضحاك بن مزاحم: اليسر الفطر في السفر والعسر الصوم في السفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording should encompass ease and hardship throughout religious matters.
rows.anchor: والوجه عموم اللفظ في جميع أمور الدين

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet described God’s religion as easy.
rows.anchor: وقد فسر ذلك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «دين الله يسر»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who missed days because of travel or illness are to complete the corresponding number of days.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ولتكملوا العدة معناه وليكمل من أفطر في سفره

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Bakr from ʿĀṣim and some transmissions from Abu ʿAmr read litukammilū with a doubled mīm; a light mīm is also transmitted and is the majority reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم وأبو عمرو في بعض ما روي عنه «ولتكملوا» بتشديد الميم

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basrans attach the lām to yurīdu as an object lām, with an implied an after the verb; Qays Kathīr ibn Ṣakhr’s line illustrates it.
rows.anchor: هذه اللام متعلقة إما ب يريد فهي اللام الداخلة على المفعول

rows.speaker: بعض الكوفيين
rows.claim: Some Kufans connect the lām to an omitted following verb: the dispensation was granted so people could complete the number.
rows.anchor: وإما بفعل مضمر بعد، تقديره ولأن تكملوا العدة رخص لكم هذه الرخصة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the lām may be imperative, with the wāw coordinating one sentence with another.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون هذه اللام لام الأمر والواو عاطفة جملة كلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to magnify God urges takbīr at the end of Ramadan.
rows.anchor: وقوله: ولتكبروا الله حض على التكبير في آخر رمضان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says takbīr begins at crescent sighting and lasts until the sermon ends; one pauses when the imam goes out, then repeats his takbīr.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: «يكبر المرء من رؤية الهلال إلى انقضاء الخطبة

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another view starts takbīr at crescent sighting and continues until the imam leaves for prayer.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: يكبر من رؤية الهلال إلى خروج الإمام إلى الصلاة

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyan takes the command to mean takbīr on Eid day.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان: «هو التكبير يوم الفطر»

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Malik says takbīr runs from when a man leaves home until the imam comes out.
rows.anchor: وقال مالك: «هو من حين يخرج الرجل من منزله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars use several formulas; all are acceptable, beginning with takbīr.
rows.anchor: والجميع حسن واسع مع البدأة بالتكبير

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some take “He guided you” specifically as guidance away from Christians’ alteration of their fast.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد لما ضل فيه النصارى من تبديل صيامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A general sense of guidance is better.
rows.anchor: وتعميم الهدى جيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expectation of gratitude is phrased in terms appropriate to human beings, for God’s gift of guidance.
rows.anchor: ولعلكم تشكرون ترج في حق البشر، أي على نعمة الله في الهدى

rows.speaker: الحسن بن أبي الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says people asked whether their Lord was near, so they could speak privately, or distant, so they should call aloud.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن بن أبي الحسن: سببها أن قوما قالوا للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: أقريب ربنا

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ says that after 40:60 was revealed, people asked when they should pray, prompting this verse.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: لما نزلت وقال ربكم ادعوني أستجب لكم [غافر: 60] قال قوم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the question was where to direct supplication.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: بل قالوا إلى أين ندعو فنزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the people asked how they should supplicate.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة بل قالوا: كيف ندعو؟ فنزلت وإذا سألك عبادي

rows.speaker: المشركون
rows.claim: The polytheists objected that God could not be near when seven immense heavens lay between them and Him.
rows.anchor: روي أن المشركين قالوا لما نزل فإني قريب: كيف يكون قريبا وبيننا وبينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is near in His ability and in answering supplication.
rows.anchor: أجيب دعوة الداع إذا دعان أي فإني قريب بالإجابة والقدرة

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One interpretation qualifies the promise: God answers if He wills.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: المعنى أجيب إن شئت

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another view says each supplication receives one of three outcomes: a worldly answer, expiation, or reward stored for the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: إن الله تعالى يجيب كل الدعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These outcomes apply when supplication stays within bounds; transgression in prayer is forbidden and 7:55 forbids it.
rows.anchor: وهذا إذا كان الدعاء على ما يجب دون اعتداء، فإن الاعتداء في الدعاء ممنوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling someone whose prayers are answered praises sound judgment and avoidance of transgression; God enables prayer for what is possible.
rows.anchor: والوصف بمجاب الدعوة: وصف بحسن النظر والبعد عن الاعتداء

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed that his community would not fight among themselves, but that prayer was denied because destiny had decreed otherwise.
rows.anchor: وانظر أن أفضل البشر المصطفى محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم قد دعا أن لا يجعل بأس أمته بينهم

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء الخراساني
rows.claim: Abu Raja al-Khurasani understands the command as “let them supplicate to Me.”
rows.anchor: قال أبو رجاء الخراساني: «معناه فليدعوا لي»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author reads istajāba as “seek that I answer them,” following the request sense of istifʿāl, with rare exceptions.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق رضي الله عنه: المعنى فليطلبوا أن أجيبهم، وهذا هو باب استفعل

rows.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
rows.claim: Mujahid and others understand the command as answering God’s call to faith through obedience and action.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وغيره: المعنى فليجيبوا لي فيما دعوتهم إليه من الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ajāba and istajāba can be synonymous; a poetic line uses istajāba to mean answer.
rows.anchor: ويقال: أجاب واستجاب بمعنى، ومنه قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: أبو رجاء
rows.claim: Abu Raja takes “believe in Me” to mean believing that God answers their supplications.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: وليؤمنوا بي، قال أبو رجاء: في أني أجيب دعاءهم

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another interpretation treats the phrase as a call to faith generally.
rows.anchor: وقال غيره: بل ذلك دعاء إلى الإيمان بجملته

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read yarshudūn with open yāʾ and ḍamma on shīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور يرشدون بفتح الياء وضم الشين

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some use ḍamma on yāʾ and fatḥa on shīn; Ibn Abi ʿAbla and Abu Haywa also transmit open yāʾ with kasra on shīn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قوم بضم الياء وفتح الشين

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq and others place these verses in the episode of ʿAmr ibn al-Hadrami and Waqid, the expedition led by ʿAbd Allah ibn Jahsh.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق وغيره: نزلت هذه الآيات في شأن عمرو بن الحضرمي وواقد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thaqiftumūhum means gaining mastery over them or encountering them when able to overpower them; thaqif laqif describes someone adept at affairs.
rows.anchor: وثقفتموهم معناه أحكمتم غلبهم ولقيتموهم قادرين عليهم

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari takes the address as directed to the emigrants and the pronoun as referring to Quraysh unbelievers.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري: «الخطاب للمهاجرين، والضمير لكفار قريش»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to all believers; “they expelled you” refers to the Prophet and emigrants, expelled by a destined decree.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق رضي الله عنه: بل الخطاب لجميع المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fitna is the pressure they applied in an attempt to make believers return to unbelief.
rows.anchor: والفتنة أشد من القتل أي الفتنة التي حملوكم عليها وراموكم بها على الرجوع إلى الكفر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says being killed is less severe for a believer than undergoing fitna.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: «أي من أن يقتل المؤمن، فالقتل أخف عليه من الفتنة»

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another view says their fitna violated truth’s sanctities more gravely than killing believers, or that their unbelief and misguidance were graver than the killing they reproached.
rows.anchor: قال غيره: بل المعنى الفتنة التي فعلوا أشد في هتك حرمات الحق

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority consider the restriction superseded, so fighting was later commanded everywhere.
rows.anchor: قال الجمهور: كان هذا ثم نسخ وأمر بالقتال في كل موضع

rows.speaker: الربيع
rows.claim: Al-Rabiʿ says the restriction was abrogated by the command to fight until persecution ends.
rows.anchor: قال الربيع: نسخه وقاتلوهم حتى لا تكون فتنة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the restriction was abrogated by 9:5, commanding the killing of polytheists wherever found after the sacred months.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: نسخه قوله تعالى: فإذا انسلخ الأشهر الحرم فاقتلوا المشركين حيث وجدتموهم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid rejects abrogation: fighting in the Sacred Mosque remains forbidden unless opponents initiate it there.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: «الآية محكمة ولا يجوز قتال أحد في المسجد الحرام إلا بعد أن يقاتل

none: Bare introductory heading only; no commentary content.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the passage concerns al-Akhnas ibn Shurayq (whose name he gives as Ubay): he professed Islam, claimed sincerity, then burned Muslim crops and killed their donkeys.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: «نزلت في الأخنس بن شريق، واسمه أبي، والأخنس لقب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says it is not established that al-Akhnas ever became Muslim.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد عبد الحق رضي الله عنه: ما ثبت قط أن الأخنس أسلم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the first passage describes hypocrites who disparaged those killed at al-Rajiʿ, naming ʿAsim ibn Thabit, Khubayb, and Ibn al-Dathinna; the following verse refers to its martyrs.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: نزلت في قوم من المنافقين تكلموا في الذين قتلوا في غزوة الرجيع عاصم بن ثابت

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد وجماعة من العلماء
rows.claim: Qatada, Mujahid, and other scholars generalize the passage to anyone concealing unbelief, hypocrisy, lies, or harm while speaking otherwise.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة ومجاهد وجماعة من العلماء: نزلت هذه الآيات في كل مبطن كفر أو نفاق

words: وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِ
rows.speaker: الترمذي
rows.claim: A report cited in al-Tirmidhi from a divine book describes people with honey-sweet tongues and bitter hearts, who use religion for worldly gain and face a confounding trial.
rows.anchor: وهي تشبه ما ورد في الترمذي أن في بعض كتب الله تعالى: «أن من عباد الله قوما ألسنتهم أحلى من العسل

words: وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He calls God to witness” means the person claims, “God knows I am telling the truth.”
rows.anchor: ومعنى ويشهد الله أي يقول: الله يعلم أني أقول حقا

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة وابن محيصن
rows.claim: Abu Haywa and Ibn Muhaysin attribute the verb to God: God knows the speaker’s words contradict his reality; this reading makes the concealed evil the heart’s content.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة وابن محيصن «ويشهد الله» بإسناد الفعل إلى اسم الجلالة

words: وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority reading more sharply condemns one who deliberately adopts good speech while inwardly contradicting it; he claims goodness in his heart.
rows.anchor: والقراءة التي للجماعة أبلغ في ذمه، لأنه قوى على نفسه التزام الكلام الحسن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reads “God witnesses what is in his heart.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس «والله يشهد على ما في قلبه»

rows.speaker: أبي وابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ubayy and Ibn Masʿud read that the speaker calls God as witness to what is in his heart.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي وابن مسعود «ويستشهد الله على ما في قلبه»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-add is a fierce, stubborn disputant who twists arguments in every direction; related expressions evoke the sides of a valley, the mouth, and a draught.
rows.anchor: والألد: الشديد الخصومة الصعب الشكيمة الذي يلوي الحجج في كل جانب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet said the most hateful men to God are the stubborn disputant.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «أبغض الرجال إلى الله الألد الخصم»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-khiṣām can be the verbal noun of khāṣama or a plural of khaṣm, making the phrase mean the most forceful of adversaries.
rows.anchor: والخصام في الآية مصدر خاصم، وقيل جمع خصم ككلب وكلاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet’s line uses “a stubborn adversary” to illustrate al-add as a description of a fierce opponent.
rows.anchor: إن تحت الأحجار حزما وعزما

rows.speaker: ابن جريج وغيره
rows.claim: On the inward-action reading, tawallā means he turned aside, grew angry and proud, then schemed to bring calamity on Islam.
rows.anchor: ونحا هذا المنحى في معنى الآية ابن جريج وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward striving is likened to the striving in 53:39 and 17:19.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا السعي قول الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A poetic line about striving for Banu Malik illustrates saʿā as purposeful effort.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر: [الرجز] أسعى على حي بني مالك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: On the physical-action reading, he turns away from Muhammad, gets up, walks across the land, and corrupts it; both readings describe corruption.
rows.anchor: نحا هذا المنحى ابن عباس وغيره، وكلا السعيين فساد

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari identifies the reference as al-Akhnas burning crops and killing donkeys.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري: «المراد الأخنس في إحراقه الزرع وقتله الحمر»

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says a wrongdoer’s corruption leads God to withhold rain, destroying crops and offspring.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: «المراد أن الظالم يفسد في الأرض فيمسك الله المطر فيهلك الحرث والنسل»

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation says the corruptor kills people, ending cultivation and the generations who tend it.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد أن المفسد يقتل الناس فينقطع عمار الزرع والمنسلون

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj allows al-harth to mean women and al-nasl their offspring.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: «يحتمل أن يراد بالحرث النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is an emphatic image of corruption: worldly affairs chiefly turn on cultivation and procreation.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: والظاهر أن الآية عبارة عن مبالغة في الإفساد

rows.speaker: أكثر القراء
rows.claim: Most readers use yuhliku, coordinated with yufsidu; Ubayy’s codex adds a conjunction before it.
rows.anchor: وأكثر القراء على يهلك بضم الياء وكسر اللام وفتح الكاف

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb’s codex reads wa-li-yuhlik.
rows.anchor: وفي مصحف أبي بن كعب «وليهلك»

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some read yahliku with a ḍamma on kāf, coordinating it with yaʿjibuka, with saʿā as a future verb, or as a new sentence.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قوم «ويهلك» بضم الكاف

rows.speaker: الحسن وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو حيوة وابن محيصن
rows.claim: These readers use yahlaku with nominative al-harth and al-nasl; the same reading is transmitted from Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن وابن أبي إسحاق وأبو حيوة وابن محيصن «ويهلك» بفتح الياء وكسر اللام وضم الكاف

rows.speaker: المهدوي
rows.claim: Al-Mahdawi says Hammad ibn Salama’s transmission from Ibn Kathir has yuhliku with al-harth accusative.
rows.anchor: وحكى المهدوي أن الذي روى حماد بن سلمة عن ابن كثير إنما هو «ويهلك» بضم الياء والكاف «الحرث» بالنصب

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some read yahlak with fatḥa on yāʾ and lām and nominative al-harth, using the dialect halaka yahlak, classed as anomalous.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قوم «ويهلك» بفتح الياء واللام ورفع «الحرث» وهي لغة هلك يهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-harth literally means plowing soil; by association it also means crops and extends to trees and orchards.
rows.anchor: والحرث في اللغة شق الأرض للزراعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In 21:78, al-harth is understood in the commentaries as a vineyard.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول عز وجل إذ يحكمان في الحرث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women are called cultivation by way of metaphor.
rows.anchor: وسمي النساء حرثا على التشبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nasl derives from nasala, to emerge in succession; it also describes a bird’s successive loss of feathers.
rows.anchor: والنسل مأخوذ من نسل ينسل إذا خرج متتابعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same root appears in 21:96, describing people streaming down from every rise.
rows.anchor: ومنه قوله تعالى: وهم من كل حدب ينسلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays’s line using tansilu illustrates the root’s sense of successive emergence.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول امرئ القيس: [الطويل] فسلي ثيابي

rows.speaker: المتكلمون
rows.claim: On the theologians’ account that love means will, God does not approve corruption religiously, though corruption does occur by His will.
rows.anchor: ولا يحب معناه لا يحبه من أهل الصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This describes an arrogant unbeliever or hypocrite, full of self-importance; a believer should avoid putting another person under such pressure.
rows.anchor: هذه صفة الكافر أو المنافق الذاهب بنفسه زهوا

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: Some scholars say it is enough of a sin to answer a brother’s admonition, “mind yourself; someone like you advises me?”
rows.anchor: وقال بعض العلماء: كفى بالمرء إثما أن يقول له أخوه اتق الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿizza means invulnerability and force of spirit: pride seizes him and carries him into sin.
rows.anchor: والعزة هنا المنعة وشدة النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, pride seized him together with sin; bā has a different function on the two readings.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل لفظ الآية أن يكون أخذته العزة مع الإثم، فمعنى الباء يختلف بحسب التأويلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hasbuhu means that Hell is sufficient as punishment and recompense.
rows.anchor: و «حسبه» أي كافيه معاقبة وجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mihād is bedding a person prepares for himself, like a mattress; a poetic line equates greeting with a painful blow.
rows.anchor: والمهاد ما مهد الرجل لنفسه كأنه الفراش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse encompasses anyone who fights in God’s path, is martyred for Him, or changes a wrong.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ومن الناس من يشري نفسه الآية تتناول كل مجاهد في سبيل الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding verses appear to concern unbelievers generally; sinners sharing these traits also incur a portion of the warning.
rows.anchor: والظاهر من هذا التقسيم أن تكون الآيات قبل هذا على العموم في الكافر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the earlier verses concern hypocrites who spoke about al-Rajiʿ, this one concerns its martyrs; if they concern al-Akhnas, this one concerns the first Anṣar and Muhājirūn to believe.
rows.anchor: ومن قال إن الآيات المتقدمة هي في منافقين تكلموا في غزوة الرجيع

rows.speaker: عكرمة وغيره
rows.claim: ʿIkrima and others connect the verse to emigrants including Suhayb: pursued while leaving Mecca, he bargained away his property, migrated, and the Prophet told him his sale had profited.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة وغيره: هذه في طائفة من المهاجرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yashrī means “sells,” as in 12:20; the author cites poetry by Yazid ibn Mufarrigh as lexical evidence.
rows.anchor: ويشري معناه يبيع، ومنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Love has an added element of preference over will; corruption may be willed without such preference, since God loves only what is wholly good.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: والحب له على الإرادة مزية إيثار

rows.speaker: يزيد بن مفرغ الحميري
rows.claim: A line by Yazid ibn Mufarrigh al-Himyari supplies a poetic use of sharaytu in the discussion of the verb’s sense.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول يزيد بن مفرغ الحميري: [مجزوء الكامل]

rows.speaker: شاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses tashrī in a context of price and asking whether one will buy, illustrating the buy sense of shara.
rows.anchor: وقال الآخر: [الكامل] يعطى بها ثمنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Shurāt are named as those who sold themselves to God; some also report shara in the sense “buy,” helping explain Suhayb’s purchase of his freedom.
rows.anchor: ومن هذا تسمى الشراة كأنهم الذين باعوا أنفسهم من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the verb means “sell” in Suhayb’s case, his resolve to fight his pursuers can count as selling himself to God.
rows.anchor: اللهم إلا أن يقال إن عزم صهيب على قتالهم بيع لنفسه من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب وعلي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس
rows.claim: ʿUmar, ʿAli, and Ibn ʿAbbas apply the verse to changing wrongdoing: after the wrongdoer rejects “fear God,” the reformer offers himself to God and fights him.
rows.anchor: وتأول هذه الآية عمر بن الخطاب وعلي بن أبي طالب وابن عباس رضي الله عنهم في مغيري المنكر

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: ʿUmar gathered Qurʾān reciters, heard Ibn ʿAbbas explain “the two men fought” as rebuker and wrongdoer, then praised him.
rows.anchor: وروي أن عمر بن الخطاب كان يجمع في يوم الجمعة شبابا من القراءة فيهم ابن عباس

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة وأبو أيوب
rows.claim: When Hisham ibn ʿAmir charged the ranks at Constantinople and some called it self-destruction, Abu Hurayra and Abu Ayyub cited this verse in his defense.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو هريرة وأبو أيوب حين حمل هشام بن عامر على الصف في القسطنطينية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibtighāʾ is a purpose object (mafʿūl min ajlih).
rows.anchor: وابتغاء مفعول من أجله

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Hamza pauses on marḍāt with tāʾ; the other readers pause with hāʾ.
rows.anchor: ووقف حمزة على مرضات بالتاء والباقون بالهاء

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli explains Hamza’s pause with tāʾ as dialectal, like ṭalḥat, or as retaining tāʾ to show the understood genitive; a rajaz line supports the dialectal form.
rows.anchor: وجه وقف حمزة بالتاء إما أنه على لغة من يقول طلحت وعلقمت

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: A second account keeps tāʾ because the genitive complement is understood within the word, making the annexation visible as in connected speech.
rows.anchor: وإما أنه لما كان المضاف إليه في ضمن اللفظة ولا بد أثبت التاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s kindness to servants offers hope and urges the conduct praised in the verse, matching the warning function of the preceding threat of Hell.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: والله رؤف بالعباد ترجية تقتضي الحض على امتثال ما وقع به المدح

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع والكسائي
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, and al-Kisaʾi read al-salm with fatḥa on sīn; the remaining readers use kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع والكسائي «السلم» بفتح السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view treats the two vowelings as synonymous, referring to Islam or peaceful settlement.
rows.anchor: فقيل: هما بمعنى واحد، يقعان للإسلام

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو بن العلاء
rows.claim: Abu ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAla distinguishes kasra as Islam and fatḥa as peaceful settlement.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عمرو بن العلاء: «السلم بكسر السين الإسلام

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad rejects the distinction between the two vowelings.
rows.anchor: وأنكر المبرد هذه التفرقة

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari prefers Islam: believers were not commanded to initiate a truce; the Prophet was only told to incline to peace when the other side does.
rows.anchor: ورجح الطبري حمل اللفظة على معنى الإسلام

rows.speaker: فرقة
rows.claim: One group takes the addressees as all Muslims, commanded to remain firm and increase observance; kāffatan then encompasses all believers and all parts of the law.
rows.anchor: فقالت فرقة: جميع المؤمنين بمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, kāffatan can be a circumstantial qualifier of two elements, compared with 19:27.
rows.anchor: فتكون الحال من شيئين، وذلك جائز

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says the addressees are Jewish converts such as ʿAbd Allah ibn Salam, who wanted to honor the Sabbath and combine Torah rules with Islam.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: «بل المخاطب من آمن بالنبي من بني إسرائيل كعبد الله بن سلام

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: For ʿIkrima, kāffatan refers only to all parts of the law.
rows.anchor: ف كافة على هذا لإجزاء الشرع فقط

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the verse was revealed about the People of the Book, telling believers in Moses and Jesus to enter Islam through Muhammad.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: «نزلت الآية في أهل الكتاب»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For those who understand al-silm as Islam, kāffatan may encompass the law or addressees; if it means peace, the command means entering into payment of jizya.
rows.anchor: يراها المسالمة يقول: أمرهم بالدخول في أن يعطوا الجزية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāffa can denote a group that restrains its dissenting member.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالكافة الجماعة التي تكف مخالفها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kāffatan may qualify an omitted verbal noun, as if the command said “enter it entirely”; the qualifier remains adverbial after the noun is omitted.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن كافة نعت لمصدر محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article in al-shayṭān is generic; ʿaduww applies to one, two, or many.
rows.anchor: والألف واللام في الشيطان للجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mubīn may mean Satan made his hostility clear, or that he is manifestly an enemy; bāna and abāna can mean the same.
rows.anchor: ومبين يحتمل أن يكون بمعنى أبان عداوته

rows.speaker: جمهور الناس
rows.claim: The majority read qurūʾ on the fuʿūl pattern with hamza; Nafiʿ is reported to double wāw without hamza, and al-Hasan reads qurū with a light tanwīn.
rows.anchor: قرأ جمهور الناس «قروء» على وزن فعول، اللام همزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This waiting period serves to establish that the womb is clear, not as worship; it excludes a woman divorced before consummation, unlike the worship-based waiting period after widowhood.
rows.anchor: وحكم هذه الآية مقصده الاستبراء لا أنه عبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general term is restricted to consummated marriages, excluding pre-consummation divorces, pregnant women, those who never menstruated, and postmenopausal women.
rows.anchor: والمطلقات لفظ عموم يراد به الخصوص في المدخول بهن

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some say those categories were included by the general wording and later abrogated; the author rejects this as weak because the verse concerns menstruating women, the usual case.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: تناولهن العموم ثم نسخن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾ is a regularly recurring time, such as a star’s rising or setting or the time a wind blows; a rajaz line uses it for anger’s time.
rows.anchor: والقرء في اللغة الوقت المعتاد تردده

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told a woman to leave prayer during her aqraʾ, meaning the days of menstruation.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: «اتركي الصلاة أيام أقرائك»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Purity is also called qurʾ because it recurs and alternates with menstruation; al-Aʿsha’s poetry uses qurūʾ for women’s periods of purity.
rows.anchor: وكذلك على هذا النظر يسمى الطهر قرءا، لأنه وقت معتاد تردده

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some derive qurʾ from gathering water in a basin: the womb gathers blood during menstruation, and the body gathers it during purity.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: القرء مأخوذ من قرء الماء في الحوض

rows.speaker: أبو بكر وعمر وعثمان وعلي وابن عباس والضحاك ومجاهد والربيع وقتادة وأصحاب الرأي وجماعة كبيرة من أهل العلم
rows.claim: These authorities take the three qurūʾ as menstruations; after divorce during a non-conjugal purity, she waits three periods and exits after bathing from the third.
rows.anchor: فقال أبو بكر وعمر وعثمان وعلي وابن عباس والضحاك ومجاهد والربيع وقتادة وأصحاب الرأي

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وغيره
rows.claim: Some who take qurūʾ as menstruations say the waiting period ends as soon as she becomes pure from the third period, before bathing.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض من يقول بالحيض إذا طهرت من الثالثة انقضت العدة قبل الغسل

rows.speaker: عائشة وابن عمر ومالك وسليمان بن يسار
rows.claim: Aisha, Ibn ʿUmar, Malik, Sulayman ibn Yasar, and many scholars take qurūʾ as periods of purity; the waiting period ends when the third menstruation begins.
rows.anchor: وقالت عائشة وابن عمر وجماعة من الصحابة والتابعين ومن بعدهم منهم سليمان بن يسار ومالك: المراد الأطهار
